task.title: Expose immutable typed extension selections
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/611 by replacing a raw borrowed vector with a selection type that records in-memory enablement intent.
acceptance_criteria: Borrow selected records from exactly one immutable registry snapshot.
Expose deterministic exact-ID lookup, enumeration, length, and emptiness.
Preserve existing duplicate, absent-ID, all-or-nothing, and ordering behavior.
Keep selection distinct from activation, persisted configuration, and per-invocation permission.

attempts.summary: Established RED coverage for a typed borrowed selection.
attempts.diagnostic: The raw Vec of borrowed records had no selection-specific exact lookup or enumeration contract.
attempts.patch: Changed focused tests to require ExtensionSelection accessors for valid and empty selections.

attempts.summary: Implemented the minimal immutable selection view.
attempts.diagnostic: One exact-ID-sorted borrowed vector supports deterministic enumeration and binary-search lookup without a second index or mutable state.
attempts.patch: Added ExtensionSelection with get, extensions, len, and is_empty and returned it from registry selection.

attempts.diagnostic: The initial wording could imply an enduring enablement state even though the borrowed selection cannot survive or rebind to a replacement registry snapshot.
attempts.patch: Clarified that disablement means constructing a new omission-based selection and that selection neither persists nor grants activation or permission.

outcome.summary: Vela now represents exact-ID selection as an immutable typed view borrowed from one registry snapshot, with deterministic lookup and explicit non-activating lifecycle semantics.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30185668654 and substantive exact-head CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/612

lessons: A domain type can state lifecycle and trust boundaries that a raw collection cannot express.
Sorted borrowed storage is sufficient for deterministic enumeration and exact lookup at this scale.
Omission in a newly constructed immutable selection is simpler than premature mutable toggle policy.
Enablement intent must remain distinct from activation and caller-owned per-invocation permission.
